newsitem.title: UK: Brazil petrochems seen a strong consumption play.
newsitem.headline: Brazil petrochems seen a strong consumption play.

text.p: Brazilian Investment bank Garantia SA on Monday recommended investors look closely at the country's petrochemical sector to gain exposure to its on-going consumer boom.

Output of consumer goods and cars has been thriving thanks in part to lower interest rates in the first half of the year, while a boom in consumer credit appears to be driving the country's economic recovery in the final months of 1996.

Garantia petrochemicals analyst Oliver Mizne, meeting investors during a 10-day trip to Britain, said petrochemical stocks were potentially a good way to gain exposure since these firms were suppliers particularly to the consumer goods sector.
"Petrochemicals are a good way to play consumption," he said. "Of total output (from the chief petrochemical firms) 60 percent serves mainly the consumer goods industry."
He saw strength in the consumer sector continuing for the next five to 10 years.

Mizne conceded that many of these firms had not been particularly accessible or investor-friendly in the past, given their limited integration and complex stockholding structures, but said this was changing.
"With time they are becoming more understandable and more investable," he said, pointing to a trend towards consolidation.
Many of these firms were presently undervalued, he added.
"Stock prices are especially low today, with weak product prices, more imports and new accounting rules," he said.
"With integration and improved petrochemical prices, we will see larger companies, specific sector plays...less uncertainty in forecasts and increased liquidity."

Garantia, which last month completed a $21 million placement for Sao Paulo plastics producer Trikem, is particularly bullish on the Sao Paulo-based firm, rating it attractive following its recent incorporation of Salgema and CQR.

"The market has not yet seen all the potential upside after the integration," he said. "Spot, contract and stock prices have gone up, but Trikem has not gone up because it has not yet been seen as an integrated PVC play."

Trikem is Latin America's largest producer of PVC and the fifth largest producer in the world. Mizne said 40 percent of its shares, excluding the company's controlling group, were available while true free flow was about 20 percent.
Other stocks in the petrochemical sector were also looking cheap.
"If you have a riskier portfolio, Rhodia-Ster is undervalued," he said. "If you want a play on acquisition, look at Unipar on the asset value of the company."
Garantia rates both Rhodia-Ster and Unipar short-term neutral but long-term attractive.
Brazil's main PET maker, Rhodia-Ster gives investors exposure to companies in the soft drinks and textile sectors, while Unipar gives exposure to consumer goods and the building industry.
While Brazilian state oil monopoly Petrobras, slated for privatisation in future, has traditionally been a play on Brazil rather than on an oil company, Mizne said it too was cheap.

"I'm positive on Petrobras because its stocks are undervalued and they are not looked at too much by oil analysts," he said. "We will see more interest looking ahead." --London Newsroom +44 171 542 2734
